title: Kinematics of Motion in a Straight Line Module 2 Lesson 2: Two Body Vertical Motion custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Particle $A$ is projected vertically upwards from ground level with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. At the same instant, particle $B$ is dropped from rest from a height of $30\text{ m}$ directly above $A$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the time taken for the two particles to collide.

Particle $A$ is projected vertically upwards from ground level with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. At the same instant, particle $B$ is dropped from rest from a height of $30\text{ m}$ directly above $A$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the height above the ground at which the collision occurs.

Particle $A$ is moving vertically upwards at $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and particle $B$ is moving vertically downwards at $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along the same vertical line. Find the relative speed of approach of the two particles.

Two particles $P$ and $Q$ are projected vertically upwards from horizontal ground at the same instant with speeds of $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the distance between the two particles after $2\text{ s}$.

Particle $A$ is projected vertically upwards from the ground with speed $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Exactly $1\text{ s}$ later, particle $B$ is projected vertically upwards from the ground with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the interval of time (measured from the projection of $A$) during which both particles are moving upwards simultaneously.

Particle $A$ is dropped from rest from the top of a tall vertical tower. Exactly $1\text{ s}$ later, particle $B$ is dropped from rest from the same point. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the time elapsed from the drop of particle $A$ when the vertical separation between the two particles is $25\text{ m}$.

questions.prompt: Two particles $A$ and $B$ move along the same vertical line. Particle $A$ is projected vertically upwards from horizontal ground with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Exactly $1\text{ s}$ later, particle $B$ is dropped from rest from a height of $35\text{ m}$ above the ground. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the time elapsed from the launch of $A$ when the two particles collide, and find the height above the ground at which the collision occurs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the speeds and directions of motion of both particles at the instant when the collision occurs.

questions.prompt: Particle $P$ is projected vertically upwards from ground level with speed $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. At the same instant, particle $Q$ is projected vertically upwards from the same point on the ground with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Both particles move freely under gravity along adjacent vertical paths. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the time taken for $Q$ to reach its maximum height, and calculate the distance between $P$ and $Q$ at this instant.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Particle $Q$ returns to the ground at time $t_1$. Find $t_1$, calculate the height of $P$ at this instant, and find the speed and direction of motion of $P$ at time $t_1$.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ is projected vertically upwards from ground level with speed $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Exactly $2\text{ s}$ later, particle $B$ is projected vertically upwards from the same point on the ground with speed $u\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Both particles move freely under gravity along parallel vertical lines. The two particles are at the same height above the ground at time $t = 3\text{ s}$ after the projection of $A$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the common height of the two particles at $t = 3\text{ s}$, and find the value of $u$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the velocities of both particles at the instant they meet, and determine whether they are moving in the same direction or in opposite directions.

questions.prompt: Particle $P$ is dropped from rest from a height of $45\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. At time $T$ seconds after $P$ is dropped, particle $Q$ is projected vertically downwards from a height of $30\text{ m}$ above the ground with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Both particles strike the ground at the same instant. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the time taken for particle $P$ to reach the ground, and its speed just before impact.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the value of $T$, and find the speed with which particle $Q$ strikes the ground.

questions.prompt: Particle $P$ is projected vertically upwards from ground level with speed $16\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Exactly $0.8\text{ s}$ later, particle $Q$ is projected vertically upwards from the same point on the ground with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Both particles move freely under gravity. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the times taken for each particle to reach its highest point, measured from the instant $P$ is projected.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the complete set of values of $t$ (measured from the instant $P$ is projected) for which both particles are moving in the same direction, and state the direction of motion for each interval.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ is projected vertically upwards from ground level with speed $U\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Exactly $1\text{ s}$ later, particle $B$ is projected vertically upwards from the same point on the ground with speed $28\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Both particles move freely under gravity along adjacent vertical lines. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the two particles are at the same height above the ground at time $t = \frac{33}{38 - U}$, where $t$ is measured from the launch of $A$, and find the value of $U$ given that the particles meet at $t = 3\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using $U = 27\text{ m s}^{-1}$, find the velocities and directions of motion of both particles at the instant they meet, and determine the difference in time between their returns to the ground.

questions.prompt: A vertical tower of height $H\text{ m}$ stands on horizontal ground. At time $t = 0$, particle $P$ is projected vertically upwards from the base of the tower with speed $25\text{ m s}^{-1}$. At the same instant, particle $Q$ is dropped from rest from the top of the tower. Both particles move along the same vertical line under gravity. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the distance between the two particles at time $t$ (before they pass or hit the ground) is given by $s(t) = H - 25t$, and find the value of $H$ given that the particles pass each other while $P$ is moving upwards at a height of $20\text{ m}$ above the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using $H = 25\text{ m}$, find the speeds and directions of motion of both particles at the instant they pass, and find the distance between the particles when $P$ reaches its highest point.
